# File Templates
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/file-templates

Upload documents and presentations as reusable templates. Anyone in your workspace can then use them to generate new files in the same format and style.

File templates let you save existing documents or slide decks and reuse them as the starting point for new AI-generated files. When you start a new document or presentation in chat, you can pick a template. Langdock will generate the new file matching its format and style.

## Supported formats

Templates can be uploaded in the following formats:

| File type     | Extensions               |
| ------------- | ------------------------ |
| Presentations | `.pptx`, `.ppt`, `.potx` |
| Documents     | `.docx`, `.dotx`         |
| PDFs          | `.pdf`                   |

Maximum file size: **100 MB**

## Browsing and using templates

### Opening the template gallery

From the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction), click **All templates** in the Create New section to open the template gallery. You can also access templates directly when starting a new file in chat. Each mode (Document, Slides) shows a **Use a Template** section.

<img alt="The template gallery showing a grid of templates with filter and sort options" />

### Filtering and sorting

The gallery lets you narrow down templates by:

* **Type**: All types, Presentation, or Document
* **Ownership**: All templates, only yours, or shared with you
* **Sort**: Newest, A–Z, or most used

### Previewing a template

Click any template card to open a full-screen preview with a carousel of all pages. From the preview you can see the layout and content before committing to it.

<img alt="Full-screen template preview showing a slide carousel" />

### Using a template

Click **Use Template** in the preview to open a new chat with the template already attached. Langdock will use the template's format and style when generating your file.

<img alt="Chat mode with a template selected, showing the template name attached" />

### Attaching a template to an agent

You can also attach file templates to an agent so it always generates files in that format. In the agent editor, go to the **Actions** section, click **Add action**, and pick the template from the **File Templates** tab. To remove it, click the **X** on its card in the Actions section.

Alternatively, ask in the Agent Builder chat: *"Attach the quarterly report template to this agent"* or *"Remove the pitch deck template"*. The builder searches templates you have access to, attaches matching ones, and shows the change inline.

## Uploading a template

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the template gallery">
    In the Library, click **All templates** to open the gallery, then click the **+** button (Add template). You can also drag and drop a file directly onto the gallery dialog.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Upload your file">
    You have two ways to provide the file:

    * **From your computer**: select a file directly. Supported formats: `.pptx`, `.ppt`, `.potx`, `.docx`, `.dotx`, `.pdf` (max 100 MB).
    * **From a connected integration**: import from Google Drive, OneDrive, or another connected source using the integration picker in the upload dialog.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Wait for analysis">
    Langdock analyzes the file to extract a suggested name and description. This takes a moment. You'll see a progress indicator while it runs.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Review and save">
    Check the extracted name and instructions, edit them if needed, and click **Save**. The template is now available in the gallery for you and anyone you share it with.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<img alt="The upload review step showing extracted template name and instructions fields" />

## Managing templates

Each template card has a context menu with the following actions:

| Action   | What it does                              |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Edit     | Change the template name and instructions |
| Share    | Share with specific users or groups       |
| Download | Download the original file                |
| Delete   | Remove the template permanently           |

## Sharing templates

You can share a template with individual users or groups in your workspace. Open the share dialog from the template card's context menu, search for users or groups, and confirm.

<div>
  <img alt="Template share dialog showing user and group search" />
</div>

Template sharing follows the same permission model as Skills. There are two permissions in workspace roles that control what users can do:

* **Share with users and groups**: Enabled for everyone by default. Any user can share a template with specific people or groups.
* **Promote to workspace**: Admin-only by default. Only admins can make a template available to the entire workspace.

You can adjust these defaults in [User Management → Roles](https://app.langdock.com/settings/workspace/user-management/roles).

## Admin: enabling templates

Templates are built on top of Skills and require Skills to be enabled in your workspace. When Skills are disabled, templates will not appear in the Library or in chat.

By default, any user can share a template with specific users or groups, but only admins can promote a template to the entire workspace. You can adjust both defaults under [User Management → Roles](https://app.langdock.com/settings/workspace/user-management/roles).

<Info>
  Go to **Settings → Workspace** to manage Skills availability for your workspace.
</Info>

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="Why can't I upload a template?">
    If you do not see the upload controls in the Library or in chat, your workspace role may not include the **Create skills** permission required to upload file templates. Ask a workspace admin to check this permission under [User management → Roles](https://app.langdock.com/settings/workspace/user-management/roles).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Which template formats work best?">
    Templates work best when the structure is clear, reusable, and not overly dependent on fragile formatting. Use consistent headings, placeholders, and example content. Complex presentations or documents with strict brand layouts may require more testing and iteration.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How should I prepare a reusable template?">
    Keep the template focused on the structure you want to preserve. Remove outdated content, use clear placeholder text, and include examples for sections that should be generated. If brand assets, fonts, or layout rules matter, include them directly in the template and describe the expected output in the prompt.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why can generated documents or presentations differ from the template?">
    Generated files may differ when the model has to adapt content length, infer missing structure, or recreate formatting from ambiguous examples. More complex layouts, charts, tables, and presentations are more likely to need manual review or multiple iterations.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Folders
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/folders

Create shared folders for files you want to work on with AI in chat.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Folders icon" />
</Frame>

Instead of attaching the same files to every chat, create a folder once, add the files you need, and open it from chat with **Work in a folder**. The model can read the files in the folder, help you compare or update them, and save generated files back when you have edit access.

Use Folders for active work: preparing a report with source material, reviewing a set of spreadsheets, collecting files for a project, or creating deliverables with your team. Use [Knowledge bases](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) when you want semantic search across a larger document collection.

## Work in a folder from chat

Folders are most useful when the same set of files belongs to an ongoing task. Select a folder in chat, then ask the model to work with the files inside it.

For example, you can ask Langdock to:

* Prepare a weekly meeting from the agenda, project updates, feedback, and previous notes
* Summarize a spreadsheet and draft follow-up notes
* Create a presentation from files in the folder
* Update a document and save the result back to the folder

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open a chat">
    Start a new chat or open an existing one.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Sidebar menu with New chat selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Choose a folder">
    Click **Work in a folder** and select the folder you want to use.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Chat input with Work in a folder open and Weekly team meeting selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Work with the files in the folder">
    For example, ask the model to use the agenda, project updates, customer feedback, and previous notes to prepare the weekly team meeting. The model can summarize the files, list open questions, and draft follow-up tasks.
  </Step>
</Steps>

Any files in the selected folder are available to the chat. If you are an Editor or Owner of a folder, files generated in the chat can also be saved back to the folder.

Open image and supported document attachments directly from chat. See [Document Search](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/document-search) for document previews and [Image Analysis](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/image-analysis) for images.

## Create a folder and add files

You can create Folders from the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction). Open the Library from the left sidebar, find the Folders section, and click **Create folder**. To find an existing folder, use the search field next to **Create folder**. It filters the list by name as you type.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Folders section with the Create folder button selected" />
</Frame>

After you create a folder, add files from your computer, move files from [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files), or move eligible attachments directly from chat. Folders are built for files you actively work with in Langdock, including documents, spreadsheets, presentations, images, and generated files. The model can visually analyze images in a folder, for example to describe a screenshot or read a diagram.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Upload from computer">
    1. Open your folder
    2. Click **Upload files** or drag files into the folder
    3. Wait until the files finish uploading
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Move from Recent Files">
    1. Open [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files)
    2. Open the file menu
    3. Click **Move to folder**
    4. Choose the destination folder
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="Move from chat">
    1. Find the sent file card in chat. On desktop, hover over the card to show its actions
    2. Click **Move to folder** on the file card
    3. Choose a destination folder where you have Editor or Owner access
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

The **Move to folder** action is available only for files you uploaded or generated directly in Langdock that are not already in a Folder or Knowledge base. Files from synced integration folders cannot be moved this way.

<Note>
  Folders can contain up to **100 files** and **250 MB** total.
</Note>

## Share work with the right people

You can share folders with individuals, groups, or your entire workspace. Use Viewer access when someone should use files as context, and Editor access when they should also add, remove, or save files to your folder.

You need the **Share folders and knowledge bases with workspace** role permission to share a folder with your entire workspace.

| Permission                 | Owner | Editor | Viewer |
| -------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ------ |
| View folder and files      | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Use files in chat          | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Edit file contents         | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Add files                  | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Remove files               | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Move files into the folder | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Share with others          | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Delete folder              | ✓     |        |        |
| Transfer ownership         | ✓     |        |        |

Workspace admins have full control over all Folders. When a Folder is linked to a [Project](/en/using-langdock/chat/projects), the Project controls who can access the Folder. Such Folders cannot be shared separately.

## Choosing the right setup

Folders work best when you are actively working with a set of files. Use the options below when you want to collaborate on those files, give an Agent reference material, or search across a larger document collection.

### Use a Project to collaborate on files

Use a [Project](/en/using-langdock/chat/projects) when several people should work with the same folder together. Everyone in the Project can use the project files as shared context in chat, and people with edit access can add files or save generated files back to the project folder.

You link a folder from the project itself with **Work in a folder**, either selecting an existing folder or creating a new one.

<Info>
  Removing a folder from a project does not delete the folder or its files. You can still find them in the Library.
</Info>

<Note>
  You can only attach a Folder to a Project when you are the Owner of both. After the Folder is linked, Project permissions control access to the folder.
</Note>

Use a Library Folder when the files should stay independent from a Project and be reused across different chats.

### Attach a Folder to an Agent for reference

Attach a Library Folder when an Agent should read from the same set of files while answering. In the agent editor, click **Add action** in the Actions section, open **Folders**, and select the Library Folder. The Agent cannot change files or save generated files back to the Folder.

### Use a Knowledge base for search

Use a [Knowledge base](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) when you need to find specific information across many documents. The model searches the Knowledge base for the most relevant sections and uses them as reference.

Use a Folder when you want to work with files directly. Use a Knowledge base when you want to search a larger collection for the right answer.

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="I cannot save generated files to a folder">
    Check that you have Editor or Owner access. Viewers can use folder files as context, but cannot save generated files there.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot edit a file in a folder">
    Files open as read-only documents when you have Viewer access. Ask the folder Owner or an Editor for edit access.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot add more files">
    Folders can contain up to 100 files and 250 MB total. Remove files or choose another folder before adding more.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot find my folder when choosing Work in a folder">
    Check that you have at least Viewer access to the folder. If the folder still does not appear, check the folder name and confirm that it still exists in the Library.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot upload a file">
    Check whether the file type is supported and whether the folder has reached the 100 files or 250 MB limit. See [Supported file types](/en/using-langdock/troubleshooting/faq/supported-file-types) for the full list.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I need to search across many documents">
    Use a [Knowledge base](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) instead. Knowledge bases are built for semantic search across larger document collections.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="When should I use a folder?">
    Use folders to organize files you want to work with in Langdock, especially when several files belong to the same project or team workflow. Use Knowledge bases when the files should become a reusable searchable source for AI answers.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Are folders the same as Knowledge bases?">
    No. Folders help organize files in the Library. Knowledge bases are designed for retrieval, so Langdock can search relevant content and use it in chats, agents, workflows, or API usage.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Introduction to Library
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/introduction

The Library brings functionality related to files into one place: create new files, manage Folders and Knowledge bases, and access every file you've generated or uploaded.

<iframe title="Library overview video" />

The Library is your central hub for working with files in Langdock. It replaces scattered file access across individual chats and gives you one place to create, find, and organize everything. Whether you're starting a new document from scratch, reusing a team template, browsing files from past conversations, working in Folders, or managing Knowledge bases, it all lives here.

## The four sections

### Create New File

Start a new document, spreadsheet, or presentation directly from the Library. Clicking Document, Spreadsheet, or Presentation opens a new chat with the corresponding mode pre-selected.

<div>
  <img alt="The Create New section showing Document, Spreadsheet, and Presentation options with a templates row below" />
</div>

If your workspace has templates enabled, you'll also see a horizontal row of recently used templates here. Click **All templates** to open the full template gallery.

<Info>
  Templates are only available when Skills are enabled in your workspace. See [File Templates](/en/using-langdock/library/file-templates) for details.
</Info>

### Folders

Folders are for active file work with AI in chat. Create a folder, add files, share access, then select it from chat with **Work in a folder**. The AI can use the folder files as context and save generated files back to the folder when you have edit access. Use the search field in the Folders section to filter folders and Knowledge bases by name as you type.

<Frame>
  <img alt="The Folders section inside the Library" />
</Frame>

See [Folders](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) for details on creating, sharing, and using Folders in chat.

### Knowledge bases

Knowledge bases are searchable document collections for chat, Agents, Workflows, and the Knowledge Folder API. Use them for larger reference sets where the AI should find relevant sections through semantic search.

<Frame>
  <img alt="The Knowledge bases section inside the Library" />
</Frame>

See [Knowledge bases](/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases) for details on creating, sharing, and searching Knowledge bases.

### Recent Files

Files you create, upload, or import in Langdock appear here: documents, spreadsheets, presentations, files uploaded to chats or the Library, files imported from integrations, and files generated in Langdock.

<img alt="The Recent Files section inside the Library" />

<Info>
  Recent Files follows your workspace's chat data retention settings. When a chat is deleted, only files associated with that chat are removed from Recent Files.
</Info>

See [Recent Files](/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files) for details on browsing, previewing, and managing your files.

## Getting to the Library

Click **Library** in the left sidebar to open it.

<div>
  <img alt="The Langdock sidebar with the Library item highlighted" />
</div>

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="When should I use the Library?">
    Use the Library to find and manage files, folders, templates, and Knowledge bases in Langdock. It is the place to organize reusable file-related assets instead of searching through individual chats.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How is the Library different from a chat attachment?">
    A chat attachment is tied to the current conversation. Library items are easier to find, reuse, organize, and share depending on permissions and file type.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Knowledge bases
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/knowledge-bases

Create searchable document collections for chat, Agents, Workflows, and the Knowledge Folder API.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Knowledge base icon" />
</Frame>

Knowledge bases help you find specific information across larger document collections. Instead of opening every file in chat, add your reference material once and use the Knowledge base when you need the model to search for the most relevant sections.

Use Knowledge bases for policies, handbooks, product documentation, support articles, manuals, and other reference material. Use [Folders](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) when you want to work directly with files, compare them, update them, or save generated files back.

<Info>
  Knowledge bases were previously called Knowledge Folders. The Knowledge Folder API keeps its existing endpoint names.
</Info>

## Search a Knowledge base from chat

Knowledge bases are most useful when you need an answer from a large set of reference documents. Select a Knowledge base in chat, then ask the model to find the information you need.

For example, you can ask Langdock to:

* Find the parental leave policy in an employee handbook
* Compare onboarding guidance across several internal documents
* Answer a support question from product documentation
* Find the right security policy for a customer questionnaire

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open a chat">
    Start a new chat or open an existing one.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Sidebar menu with New chat selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Choose a Knowledge base">
    Type `@`, search for the Knowledge base, and select it from the list.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Chat input with a Knowledge base selected" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Ask a question">
    For example, ask the model to find the parental leave policy in the employee handbook. The model searches the Knowledge base for relevant sections and answers from those sources.
  </Step>
</Steps>

When you use a Knowledge base in chat, Langdock searches for relevant sections from your documents. It does not send every document to the model.

## Create a Knowledge base and add documents

You can create Knowledge bases from the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction). Open the Library from the left sidebar, find the Folders section, click the arrow next to **Create folder**, and select **Knowledge base**.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Folders section with the Create folder dropdown open and Knowledge base selected" />
</Frame>

After you create a Knowledge base, upload documents from your computer or use the Knowledge Folder API for automated uploads. Knowledge bases are built for text-based reference material that should be searched later.

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Upload from computer">
    1. Open your Knowledge base
    2. Click **Upload files** or drag documents into the Knowledge base
    3. Wait until the files finish processing
  </Tab>

  <Tab title="API upload">
    Use the Knowledge Folder API when you need to upload, update, delete, retrieve, or search files programmatically. For write operations, the API key itself needs the Editor role on the Knowledge base. The Viewer role covers search and retrieval.

    See the [Knowledge Folder API reference](/en/developer/knowledge-folder-api/sharing) for authentication, rate limits, and endpoint details.
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

<Warning>
  Knowledge bases accept supported text-based formats such as PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, and presentations. They do not accept tabular files, images, or audio.
</Warning>

<Note>
  Knowledge bases can contain up to **1,000 files**. Each file can contain up to **8 million characters**.
</Note>

## Share search access with the right people

You can share Knowledge bases with individuals, groups, or your entire workspace. Use Viewer access when someone should search documents, and Editor access when they should also add, remove, or manage documents.

You need the **Share folders and knowledge bases with workspace** role permission to share a Knowledge base with your entire workspace.

| Permission                        | Owner | Editor | Viewer |
| --------------------------------- | ----- | ------ | ------ |
| View Knowledge base and documents | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Search documents in chat          | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Use in Agents                     | ✓     | ✓      | ✓      |
| Add documents                     | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Remove documents                  | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Share with others                 | ✓     | ✓      |        |
| Delete Knowledge base             | ✓     |        |        |
| Transfer ownership                | ✓     |        |        |

Workspace admins have full control over all Knowledge bases.

## Convert a Knowledge base to a folder

If you started with a Knowledge base but want to work with the files directly instead of searching them, you can convert it to a regular [folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders). Files and sharing access move to the new folder, and the original Knowledge base is removed.

Convert a Knowledge base when you want to:

* Open files in chat, compare them, or edit them
* Save generated files back to the same location
* Add spreadsheets, images, or other file types that Knowledge bases don't accept

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Knowledge base">
    In the [Library](/en/using-langdock/library/introduction), open the Knowledge base you want to convert. You need Editor or Owner access.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Select Convert to folder">
    Open the more actions menu and select **Convert to folder**.
  </Step>

  <Step title="Confirm the conversion">
    Review the confirmation dialog, then confirm. The files and existing sharing access move to a new folder, and the Knowledge base is removed.
  </Step>
</Steps>

<Note>
  Folders have lower limits than Knowledge bases: up to **100 files** and **250 MB** total. If your Knowledge base has more files, remove some before converting.
</Note>

<Warning>
  You can't convert a Knowledge base that's still connected through API access, Assistants, chats, or Automations. Remove those connections first, then try again.
</Warning>

## Choosing the right setup

Knowledge bases work best when you need to search across many documents. Use the options below when you want to work directly with files or give an Agent access to the same reference material.

### Use a Folder to work with files

Use a [Folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) when you want to open files in chat, compare them, update them, or save generated files back. Folders are better for active work with a smaller set of files.

Use a Knowledge base when you want to search a larger collection for the right answer.

### Add a Knowledge base to an Agent for search

Add a Knowledge base to an [Agent](/en/using-langdock/agents/configuration) when the Agent should search the same reference material while answering. In the agent editor, click **Add action** in the Actions section, open **Folders**, and select the Knowledge base.

Use the Knowledge section for files uploaded from your computer, individual files from integrations, and synced folders from SharePoint or Google Drive.

## FAQ

<AccordionGroup>
  <Accordion title="My Knowledge base is not appearing in @mentions">
    Check that you have at least Viewer access, then type more of the Knowledge base name to narrow the results.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="The model is not finding relevant information">
    Check that your documents finished processing, then rephrase your question with more specific terms. Verify that the information exists in the uploaded documents.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="I cannot upload certain file types">
    Knowledge bases accept supported text-based formats such as PDF, DOCX, TXT, Markdown, and presentations. Use a [Folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) when you need to work with spreadsheets, images, audio, or generated files.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="What should go into a Knowledge base instead of a direct attachment?">
    Use a Knowledge base for information that should be reused across chats, agents, workflows, or API usage. It is best for larger or longer-lived document collections where Langdock should search relevant sections instead of sending every file in full each time.
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="How fresh is Knowledge base content?">
    Uploaded Knowledge base content is available after processing. If recent content is missing, check the processing status before assuming the model ignored the file. For automatically updated content, use [Folder Sync](/en/using-langdock/guides/integrations/folder-sync).
  </Accordion>

  <Accordion title="Why are some files not searchable in a Knowledge base?">
    Files may not be searchable if the format is unsupported, the file failed processing, the content cannot be extracted reliably, or the source permissions prevent access. Spreadsheets and tabular data are not supported by Knowledge bases and should be used directly in chat instead.
  </Accordion>
</AccordionGroup>


# Recent Files
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/library/recent-files

Access every file generated or uploaded in your Langdock workspace from one place. Preview, download, organize, and manage files without digging through individual chats.

Recent Files shows files you create, upload, or import in Langdock. Documents, spreadsheets, presentations, files uploaded to chats or the Library, and files imported from connected integrations all appear here.

<img alt="Recent Files in grid view showing file thumbnails with names and metadata" />

## What appears in Recent Files

Recent Files shows files based on their origin:

| Origin        | What it includes                                         |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Generated** | Documents and presentations created by Langdock in chat  |
| **Uploaded**  | Files uploaded directly to a conversation or the Library |
| **Imported**  | Files pulled in from connected integrations              |

Files stored in Folders and workflow-only files are not shown here.

<Info>
  Recent Files follows your workspace's chat data retention settings. When a chat is deleted, only files associated with that chat are removed from Recent Files.
</Info>

## Grid and list view

Toggle between grid view (thumbnails) and list view (rows with details) using the view switcher in the top-right corner of the Recent Files section. Your preference is saved automatically.

## Filtering

Use the filter controls to narrow down files:

* **File type**: Documents, Presentations, or PDFs
* **Date**: Filter by creation date range
* **Origin**: Uploaded, Generated, or Imported

## File actions

Each file has a set of actions available from its context menu or action bar:

| Action         | Description                                                          |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Preview        | Open a preview of the file                                           |
| Download       | Download the file; generated documents offer Word, PDF, and Markdown |
| Jump to chat   | Open the original chat when the file came from a chat                |
| Start chat     | Open a new chat with this file attached                              |
| Move to folder | Move the file into a Folder                                          |
| Delete         | Remove the file permanently                                          |

## File preview

Files can be previewed in these ways:

**Inline thumbnail.** Visible directly on each file card in grid view.

**Side panel.** Click a file to open a resizable side panel preview without leaving the Library.

**Full-screen.** Open the full-screen view for a larger preview. Multi-page files (documents, presentations) show a slide thumbnail strip for quick navigation. Presentations also support a presenter mode.

**Spreadsheet preview.** Open spreadsheets with sheet tabs, zoom, column resizing, and formula inspection.

## Batch actions

Select multiple files to enable batch actions in one of these ways:

* **Shift + click** to select a range of files
* In list view, hover over the list and click the checkbox in the header to select every file in the current view

Once files are selected, a bar appears at the bottom with options to:

* **Select all** to extend the selection to every visible file
* **Download** all selected files
* **Move to folder**: moves all selected files into a Folder at once
* **Delete** all selected files

<Tip>
  With **Select all**, you select every visible file that matches your active filters. Narrow the list by file type, date, or origin before applying a batch action.
</Tip>

## Moving files to a Folder

From any file's context menu, select **Move to folder** and choose the destination Folder. You can also drag files onto a Folder or Knowledge base, or do this in bulk using batch selection.

Once moved, the file is accessible within that Folder and can be used for AI search via @mentions in chat.


# Excel Plugin
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/microsoft-plugins/excel

With the Excel plugin you can work with Langdock without leaving your Excel workbook.

<iframe title="Excel Plugin overview" />

The Excel plugin brings Langdock into Microsoft Excel, so your spreadsheets and AI assistance stay side by side. Use it to understand workbooks faster, create formulas, clean up data, and turn spreadsheet findings into clear summaries without switching tools. You can ask questions while looking at your workbook, iterate on outputs directly in Excel, and keep your analysis in the place where the work is happening.

## How to install Langdock for Excel

Install the Langdock Add-in from the Microsoft Marketplace and connect it to your Langdock account.

<Note>
  Before you can sign in, an admin needs to enable the Excel plugin in the workspace integration settings. If it is not enabled yet, point your admin to the [Plugin Setup Guide](/en/admin/manage-integrations/plugin-setup-guides/excel).
</Note>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Open the Microsoft Marketplace">
    Navigate to the [Langdock for Excel](https://marketplace.microsoft.com/en-us/product/office/WA200011245?tab=Overview) page on the Microsoft Marketplace.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Excel listing on the Microsoft Marketplace with the Get it now button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Get the Add-in">
    Click **Get it now** and confirm your details in the dialog that appears.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Confirm your details dialog for Langdock for Excel with the Get it now button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open in Excel">
    Click **Open in Excel** to launch the Add-in directly in your workbook.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Excel launch page with the Open in Excel button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Sign in to Langdock">
    Follow the sign-in flow to connect the Add-in to your Langdock account. Click **Continue** to log in.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock sign-in screen for Microsoft Excel with the Continue button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>
</Steps>

You can now use Langdock while your workbook stays open. Start with a specific question about what you want to understand, calculate, clean up, or explain.

## Working with Langdock in Excel

The Excel plugin is useful whenever the work starts in a spreadsheet. Instead of copying data into a separate chat, you can keep Excel open and use Langdock alongside it.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Excel plugin card showing the Excel icon and text Use Langdock inside of Microsoft Excel" />
</Frame>

### Common use cases

* **Build tables and plans**: Ask Langdock to create budget plans, project trackers, comparison tables, reporting templates, or charts directly in your workbook.
* **Create calculations**: Describe the calculation you need and let Langdock add formulas, totals, percentages, or growth rates.
* **Clean and structure data**: Standardize names, dates, categories, currencies, or messy rows before you analyze them.
* **Analyze spreadsheet results**: Ask Langdock to find trends, outliers, changes, and key takeaways in your data.
* **Research and enrichment**: Use Langdock to research companies, markets, or topics and add useful context to your spreadsheet.
* **Prepare summaries**: Turn spreadsheet findings into updates for reports, emails, presentations, or team meetings.

### Example: Build a quarterly budget plan

Say you need to create a quarterly budget plan with department-level cost breakdowns. Open the Langdock Add-in next to your workbook and describe what you want to build.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Excel workbook with the Langdock Add-in open next to an empty spreadsheet" />
</Frame>

Ask Langdock for the spreadsheet you need:

`Build a quarterly budget plan with department-level cost breakdowns`

<Frame>
  <img alt="Langdock Add-in in Excel with a prompt asking for a quarterly budget plan with department-level cost breakdowns" />
</Frame>

Langdock creates the table in your workbook and keeps the conversation open next to it. From there, you can ask follow-up questions, analyze the table, perform calculations, or use connected integrations without leaving Excel.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Excel workbook with a quarterly budget table and Langdock summarizing the results in the Add-in panel" />
</Frame>

### Jump to cited cells

When Langdock references cells in a reply, the reference appears as a clickable pill, for example **Sheet1 B3:B8**. Click the pill to open the referenced sheet and select the range in your workbook. If the sheet has since been renamed or removed, Langdock shows a short notice instead.

### Import an uploaded spreadsheet

Attach a spreadsheet to the chat and ask Langdock to open, import, insert, or edit it in Excel, for example `Import this spreadsheet into my workbook`. Langdock copies the attached workbook's sheets into the workbook you have open so you can review and edit them in place. Without an explicit request, the attachment stays a read-only data source and your workbook stays unchanged. Importing never modifies the uploaded file or its source in OneDrive, SharePoint, or Google Drive.

### Next steps

After Langdock creates the first output, you can keep working from the same panel:

* Ask follow-up questions about the sheet
* Add calculations, totals, or comparisons
* Enrich the spreadsheet with results from a [Web Search](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/web-search)
* Draft an email by using [Actions in Chat](/en/using-langdock/chat/tools/actions-in-chat) and selecting your email provider from your connected [integrations](/en/using-langdock/integrations/introduction)

## Edit permissions

Langdock asks before changing your workbook by default. Switch modes from the **Edit permissions** menu in the chat input:

* **Ask before edits**: Langdock shows a confirmation with the action, target range, and cell count before each write. Choose **Allow once**, **Always allow**, or **Deny**.
* **Accept all edits**: Langdock applies edits without asking.

In both modes, Langdock never overwrites populated cells unless the request is explicitly a replacement. Otherwise it proposes a different range or asks you to confirm. Formulas that fetch external data or open links are always rejected.

## Save to Library

You can save files from the Excel plugin directly to your Langdock Library, making them accessible to your Workspace and team. Save to the Library root or choose a specific [Folder](/en/using-langdock/library/folders) to organize files for everyone with access.

<Frame>
  <img alt="Save to Library dropdown in the Excel plugin" />
</Frame>

## Preferences

Open the plugin menu in the top bar and select **Preferences** to customize the plugin. In the **Instructions** field, add custom instructions that apply only to chats in the Excel plugin, for example `Round decimals to two places`. Below that, choose a **Default model** that is preselected whenever you start a new plugin chat. Both are independent of your global [account settings](/en/using-langdock/account/account). You can also switch the theme and delete all plugin conversations here.


# Outlook Plugin
Source: https://docs.langdock.com/en/using-langdock/microsoft-plugins/outlook

With the Outlook plugin you can work with Langdock without leaving your Outlook inbox or calendar.

The Outlook plugin brings Langdock into Microsoft Outlook, so your email, calendar, and AI assistance stay side by side. Use it to catch up on a full inbox, get the key points from long threads, draft replies, and prepare your meetings without switching tools. Langdock knows which email or calendar event you have open, so you can ask about it directly instead of copying content into a separate chat.

## How to install Langdock for Outlook

Install the Langdock Add-in from the Microsoft Marketplace and connect it to your Langdock account. The plugin is available in Outlook on the web and desktop.

<Note>
  Before you can sign in, an admin needs to enable the Outlook plugin in the workspace integration settings. If it is not enabled yet, point your admin to the [Plugin Setup Guide](/en/admin/manage-integrations/plugin-setup-guides/outlook).
</Note>

<Steps>
  <Step title="Get the Add-in">
    Navigate to the Langdock for Outlook page on the Microsoft Marketplace, click **Get it now**, and confirm your details in the dialog that appears.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Outlook listing on the Microsoft Marketplace with the Get it now button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Open in Outlook">
    After the Add-in is added to your account, click **Open in Outlook Web**.

    <Frame>
      <img alt="Langdock for Outlook confirmation page with the Open in Outlook Web button" />
    </Frame>
  </Step>

  <Step title="Sign in to Langdock">
    Return to your inbox, open an email, and click **Langdock** in the Outlook toolbar. Without an open email, the apps in the toolbar are disabled. Click **Continue** and sign in through your browser. Copy the sign-in code, paste it into the **Complete sign-in** screen in Outlook, then click **Continue**.

Skipping the connection is fine, you can always catch up on it later. Until then, Langdock only sees the subject and participants of the open email or event.
